learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of basic anatomical knowledge to understand the general organization of the human body with particular attention to morphology and biomechanics.
Know in depth the macroscopic and microscopic anatomy.
Know the systematic and functional organization of human body systems and systems.
Be able to remember the fundamental concepts to discuss the correlations between the structures of the human body and their functions.
Be able to apply anatomical knowledge and understanding technical aspects.
Have acquired the basic anatomical-medical terminology.
Have acquired the skills necessary for the professional opportunities provided by the degree course.

syllabus_topics: Organization of the human body and anatomical terminology
General information on bones, joints and muscles
Common cavities of the skull and splanchnocranium
Analysis of the architecture of the skull
Joints of the head and spine
Temporomandibular joint (TMJ)- general organization- movements and biomechanics
oral vestibule- lips, cheeks, gingival-dental arches
oral cavity proper- hard palate, soft palate- floor, sublingual groove- oral mucosa, gums
Greater salivary glands: structure, relationships, loggias
Nose: external nose and nasal cavities
Trachea and bronchi: relationships and structure
NEW BIOMEDICAL TECHNOLOGIES Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
teaching_methods: Multimedia classroom with virtual dissection table
assessment_rules: The exam aims to ascertain the student's knowledge and ability to describe the structural organization of the human body and structure-function relationships. The final assessment is based on a multiple-choice written test consisting of 31 quizzes, each with 4 possible answers and one correct option. The time allotted for the test is 30 minutes. Grading follows the rule: 1 point for each correct answer; 0 points for incorrect or unanswered questions. Grades are expressed in thirtieths, ranging from 18 to 30 cum laude. A student fails if they do not possess the minimum required knowledge of the main course content.
